This page demonstrates practical weather data analysis using weathervault.

## Temperature Analysis

### Daily Temperature Range

Calculate and visualize daily temperature ranges:

```{python}
import weathervault as wv
import polars as pl

# Get hourly data for a full year
weather = wv.get_weather_data("725030-14732", years=2024, make_hourly=True)

# Calculate daily min/max/mean temperatures
daily_temps = weather.group_by_dynamic("time", every="1d").agg([
    pl.col("temp").min().alias("min_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").max().alias("max_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").mean().alias("mean_temp"),
]).with_columns([
    (pl.col("max_temp") - pl.col("min_temp")).alias("temp_range")
])

# Find days with largest temperature swings
print("Days with largest temperature swings:")
daily_temps.sort("temp_range", descending=True).head(10)
```

### Monthly Temperature Trends

```{python}
# Monthly average temperatures
monthly = weather.group_by_dynamic("time", every="1mo").agg([
    pl.col("temp").mean().alias("mean_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").min().alias("min_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").max().alias("max_temp"),
])

monthly
```

### Temperature Distribution by Month

```{python}
# Temperature statistics by month
monthly_dist = weather.group_by(pl.col("time").dt.month()).agg([
    pl.col("temp").mean().alias("mean"),
    pl.col("temp").median().alias("median"),
    pl.col("temp").std().alias("std"),
    pl.col("temp").quantile(0.25).alias("q25"),
    pl.col("temp").quantile(0.75).alias("q75"),
]).sort("time")

monthly_dist
```

## Wind Analysis

### Wind Speed Statistics

```{python}
# Wind speed analysis
wind_stats = weather.filter(pl.col("ws").is_not_null()).select([
    pl.col("ws").mean().alias("mean_wind_speed"),
    pl.col("ws").max().alias("max_wind_speed"),
    pl.col("ws").quantile(0.95).alias("wind_95th_percentile"),
])

print(wind_stats)
```

### Prevailing Wind Direction

```{python}
# Most common wind directions
wind_dirs = weather.filter(
    pl.col("wd").is_not_null()
).group_by("wd").agg([
    pl.len().alias("count")
]).sort("count", descending=True)

print("Top 5 wind directions:")
print(wind_dirs.head(5))
```

### Calm vs Windy Days

```{python}
# Classify days by wind speed
daily_wind = weather.group_by_dynamic("time", every="1d").agg([
    pl.col("ws").mean().alias("mean_wind_speed"),
    pl.col("ws").max().alias("max_wind_speed"),
])

calm_days = daily_wind.filter(pl.col("mean_wind_speed") < 2).height
windy_days = daily_wind.filter(pl.col("mean_wind_speed") > 5).height

print(f"Calm days (< 2 m/s): {calm_days}")
print(f"Windy days (> 5 m/s): {windy_days}")
```

## Humidity and Comfort

### Relative Humidity Distribution

```{python}
# Humidity statistics by season
weather_with_season = weather.with_columns([
    pl.col("time").dt.month().alias("month")
]).with_columns([
    pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in([12, 1, 2])).then(pl.lit("Winter"))
    .when(pl.col("month").is_in([3, 4, 5])).then(pl.lit("Spring"))
    .when(pl.col("month").is_in([6, 7, 8])).then(pl.lit("Summer"))
    .otherwise(pl.lit("Fall"))
    .alias("season")
])

seasonal_humidity = weather_with_season.group_by("season").agg([
    pl.col("rh").mean().alias("mean_humidity"),
    pl.col("rh").min().alias("min_humidity"),
    pl.col("rh").max().alias("max_humidity"),
])

seasonal_humidity
```

### Heat Index Calculation

Calculate apparent temperature combining heat and humidity:

```{python}
# Simplified heat index formula (Fahrenheit)
# HI = c1 + c2*T + c3*RH + c4*T*RH + c5*T^2 + c6*RH^2 + c7*T^2*RH + c8*T*RH^2 + c9*T^2*RH^2

def calculate_heat_index(temp_c, rh):
    """Calculate heat index from temperature (C) and relative humidity (%)."""
    # Convert to Fahrenheit
    T = (temp_c * 9/5) + 32
    RH = rh

    # Rothfusz regression (valid for T >= 80°F, RH >= 40%)
    HI = (
        -42.379 +
        2.04901523 * T +
        10.14333127 * RH -
        0.22475541 * T * RH -
        0.00683783 * T * T -
        0.05481717 * RH * RH +
        0.00122874 * T * T * RH +
        0.00085282 * T * RH * RH -
        0.00000199 * T * T * RH * RH
    )

    # Convert back to Celsius
    return (HI - 32) * 5/9

# Calculate heat index for summer
summer = weather_with_season.filter(
    pl.col("season") == "Summer"
).filter(
    pl.col("temp").is_not_null() & pl.col("rh").is_not_null()
)

# Find hot, humid days
hot_humid = summer.filter(
    (pl.col("temp") > 27) & (pl.col("rh") > 60)
).select([
    "time", "temp", "rh"
])

print(f"Hot and humid observations: {hot_humid.height}")
hot_humid.head(10)
```

## Precipitation Indicators

While ISD data doesn't directly provide precipitation amounts, we can infer wet conditions from high humidity and low visibility:

```{python}
# Identify likely precipitation events
wet_conditions = weather.filter(
    (pl.col("rh") > 95) &
    (pl.col("visibility") < 5000)  # Less than 5km visibility
).select([
    "time", "temp", "rh", "visibility"
])

print(f"Observations with likely precipitation: {wet_conditions.height}")
wet_conditions.head(10)
```

## Multi-Station Comparison

Compare weather patterns across nearby stations:

```{python}
# Get data for three NYC airports
lga = wv.get_weather_data("725030-14732", years=2024, incl_stn_info=True)
jfk = wv.get_weather_data("744860-94789", years=2024, incl_stn_info=True)
ewr = wv.get_weather_data("725020-14734", years=2024, incl_stn_info=True)

# Combine
nyc = pl.concat([lga, jfk, ewr])

# Compare temperature statistics
comparison = nyc.group_by(["id", "name"]).agg([
    pl.col("temp").mean().alias("mean_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").std().alias("std_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").min().alias("min_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").max().alias("max_temp"),
    pl.len().alias("num_obs"),
])

comparison
```

### Temperature Differences

```{python}
# Align data by hour and calculate differences
# (simplified - assumes matching timestamps)
lga_hourly = lga.filter(pl.col("temp").is_not_null()).select([
    "time", pl.col("temp").alias("lga_temp")
]).sort("time")

jfk_hourly = jfk.filter(pl.col("temp").is_not_null()).select([
    "time", pl.col("temp").alias("jfk_temp")
]).sort("time")

# Join on time
temp_diff = lga_hourly.join(jfk_hourly, on="time").with_columns([
    (pl.col("lga_temp") - pl.col("jfk_temp")).abs().alias("temp_difference")
])

print(f"Mean temperature difference: {temp_diff['temp_difference'].mean():.2f}°C")
print(f"Max temperature difference: {temp_diff['temp_difference'].max():.2f}°C")
```

## Historical Trends

Analyze long-term climate trends:

```{python}
# Get multiple years of data
years = [2022, 2023, 2024]
historical = wv.get_weather_data("725030-14732", years=years)

# Annual average temperatures
annual = historical.group_by(pl.col("time").dt.year()).agg([
    pl.col("temp").mean().alias("mean_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").min().alias("min_temp"),
    pl.col("temp").max().alias("max_temp"),
]).sort("time")

annual
```

### Warming Trends

```{python}
# Calculate linear trend (simplified)
annual_means = annual["mean_temp"].to_list()
years_numeric = list(range(len(annual_means)))

# Simple difference between first and last 5 years
first_5_years = sum(annual_means[:5]) / 5
last_5_years = sum(annual_means[-5:]) / 5

print(f"First 5 years average: {first_5_years:.2f}°C")
print(f"Last 5 years average: {last_5_years:.2f}°C")
print(f"Change: {last_5_years - first_5_years:+.2f}°C")
```

## Extreme Weather Events

### Heat Waves

Identify prolonged periods of high temperatures:

```{python}
# Daily maximum temperatures
daily_max = weather.group_by_dynamic("time", every="1d").agg([
    pl.col("temp").max().alias("max_temp")
])

# Find consecutive hot days (> 30°C)
hot_threshold = 30
hot_days = daily_max.filter(pl.col("max_temp") > hot_threshold)

print(f"Days exceeding {hot_threshold}°C: {hot_days.height}")
hot_days.head(10)
```

### Cold Snaps

```{python}
# Daily minimum temperatures
daily_min = weather.group_by_dynamic("time", every="1d").agg([
    pl.col("temp").min().alias("min_temp")
])

# Find freezing days
freezing_days = daily_min.filter(pl.col("min_temp") < 0)

print(f"Days with freezing temperatures: {freezing_days.height}")
freezing_days.head(10)
```

## Data Quality Assessment

### Observation Frequency

```{python}
# Calculate time gaps between observations
weather_sorted = weather.sort("time")

time_diffs = weather_sorted.select([
    pl.col("time"),
    pl.col("time").diff().dt.total_minutes().alias("minutes_since_last")
])

# Distribution of observation intervals
print(time_diffs["minutes_since_last"].describe())
```

### Data Completeness by Variable

```{python}
# Calculate completeness percentage for each variable
completeness = pl.DataFrame({
    "variable": ["temp", "dew_point", "rh", "wd", "ws", "atmos_pres", "ceil_hgt", "visibility"],
    "completeness_%": [
        (weather["temp"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["dew_point"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["rh"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["wd"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["ws"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["atmos_pres"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["ceil_hgt"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
        (weather["visibility"].is_not_null().sum() / weather.height * 100),
    ]
}).sort("completeness_%", descending=True)

completeness
```

## Exporting for Visualization

Prepare data for plotting with other libraries:

```{python}
# Create a clean dataset for visualization
viz_data = weather.select([
    "time",
    "temp",
    "dew_point",
    "rh",
    "ws",
]).filter(
    pl.col("temp").is_not_null()
)

# Save to CSV for use with matplotlib, seaborn, plotly, etc.
viz_data.write_csv("weather_viz_data.csv")
```
